profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Chandler, Arizona. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company acquired 55.9 acres in Chandler in September 2011 for data center construction, part of its early 2010s national expansion under Cincinnati Bell ownership. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PHX1 publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across 2,000,000 square feet of technical space in Chandler, Arizona. That figure leads all Arizona facilities this site has read: it represents roughly 33 percent of the 512 MW published across the four Arizona campuses with disclosed figures, out of 56 mapped facilities in the state, most of which publish no capacity number at all. At 40 kW per rack, a common assumption for AI training density, 169 MW of IT load is roughly 4,225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common assumption for general enterprise colocation, the same load is roughly 16,900 racks. The arithmetic is the assumption, not the operator's claim.

The certifications qualify the campus for specific categories of regulated workload. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for tenants with financial and operational controls audit requirements. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 qualifies it for organizations requiring a recognized information security management standard. FISMA qualifies it for federal agency workloads subject to that framework. TIA-942 attests to a recognized data center design and construction standard. Green Globes attests to a published environmental performance rating.

For an AI decision, the relevant facts are the scale and the location. A 169 MW campus is large enough to absorb the power draw of a meaningful AI training cluster, and it sits in a metro area that has drawn significant data center investment. Arizona's grid situation and water availability for cooling are constraints that matter to AI at this power level, but neither is addressed in the published specifications, so this site cannot characterize them from the operator's own data.
